findings.title: Whole-row JSON string compare can conflict permanently if the stored payload doesn't round-trip
findings.body: `writeIfProviderThreadUnchanged` compares the stored `payload_json` text with `encodeProviderThreadPayload(expected)`, where `expected` was decoded from that row. `OrchestrationV2ProviderThread` (packages/contracts/src/orchestrationV2.ts:978-990) fills decoding defaults for `pendingBackgroundTasks`, `contextUsage`, `nativeMetadata` and `goal`. A row written without those keys (written before the fields existed, or by a writer that omitted them) decodes with the defaults and re-encodes to a different string than the stored one. The compare then fails on every attempt, so `writeReleasedBackgroundWorkEvents` (ProviderSessionManager.ts:846-883) exhausts its 3 attempts, logs a warning, and leaves the roster in place, which is the Waiting state this change is meant to fix. A row that has a non-empty roster was most likely written recently by the live session, so this is unlikely in practice. Still, the CAS depends on decode→encode being byte-stable. Consider comparing a canonical decoded form, or add a test that seeds a row with the optional keys omitted.

contracts.action: On session release (detach-triggered, idle, close), clear pending background tasks from the released session's provider threads
contracts.equivalent_path: writeReleasedSessionEvents / writeReleasedRuntimeRequestEvents (same release-records path) settle the session status and runtime requests the same way after the scope closes
contracts.before_after: Before: the roster stayed after the process died, so the thread stayed Waiting. After: the roster is read right after the live entry is removed (before scope close), then removed from the stored rosters inside writeReleaseRecords, with retry via retryReleaseRecords. Clearing is idempotent: a second run finds no matching task ids and returns.
contracts.visible_effect: Settled and idle-released Claude and Muse threads stop showing Waiting. Other runtimes are untouched because the flag is opt-in.
contracts.failure_mode: A read failure is caught, logged, and treated as no tasks. A roster write failure fails writeReleaseRecords and triggers the existing retry loop. CAS conflicts retry 3 times, then log and give up, leaving the roster. Server shutdown deliberately skips this because startup recovery handles it.

contracts.action: New EventSink.writeIfProviderThreadUnchanged compare-and-set on the stored provider-thread payload_json
contracts.equivalent_path: writeIfProviderThreadOwner (EventSink.ts:473-527) and writeIfRunCurrent (EventSink.ts:413-471): same commitThenPublish shape with a guard SELECT inside the transaction
contracts.before_after: Siblings compare structured columns (activeAttemptId, lastRunOrdinal, status). The new one compares the full payload_json string written by the same encoder in ProjectionStore.ts:2204. Like the siblings, it normalizes, appends, applies stored events, and publishes only when committed. It skips effect-outbox enqueue and the guardUserInputCancellations option, which is fine for a provider-thread event.
contracts.visible_effect: A concurrent replacement-session update is never overwritten by the cleanup. The cleanup re-reads and retries.
contracts.failure_mode: If the stored row does not round-trip through decode→encode, the compare always fails and the cleanup gives up after 3 attempts with a warning (see finding). A missing row is also reported as not committed.

contracts.action: The roster of threads to clear is derived from attachedThreadIds plus the detached thread
contracts.equivalent_path: mcpCredentialIdByThread revocation in releaseEntry also covers threads that detached earlier without re-attaching, which attachedThreadIds does not
contracts.before_after: Threads that detached earlier from a still-live multi-thread session are no longer in attachedThreadIds, so their tasks would not be cleared on the later release. Only Claude and Muse opt in, and both declare supportsMultipleProviderThreadsPerSession: false, so there is at most one attached thread and this gap cannot occur today.
contracts.failure_mode: A future multi-thread runtime that sets backgroundTasksEndWithProcess would leave detached threads' rosters behind. The flag's doc comment doesn't mention this limit.

summary: The change is sound. On release of a Claude or Muse session (detach, idle, close; not server shutdown), it reads the session's background-task rosters before a replacement can open, then removes only those task ids via a compare-and-set write with 3 retries. Both opted-in runtimes are single-thread, so using attachedThreadIds plus the detached thread covers them. The one point worth a look is that the compare is a byte-for-byte match of decoded-then-re-encoded JSON, which would conflict permanently on a row that doesn't round-trip; I rate that unlikely and low-confidence. The new tests cover detach, idle, opt-out, replacement and race cases. I found no other defects.
